automated.summary: All four required leaves for statement-export-api execute and pass, each proven by the junit report naming the LEAF rather than by an exit code (D-0024). Beyond the unit leaves, a REAL workbook was generated through the running route and reopened with exceljs, which is what caught the one defect the tests did not: POST api/mis/statement/export returned 200 with the xlsx content type and Content-Disposition attachment; filename="financial-mis-agriculture-nursery-dub-2026-07-01-to-2026-07-01.xlsx", matching the canonical slug grammar. Reopened, the workbook is worksheet 'Financial MIS' with 109 rows: merged identity and per-block header groups on row 1, column labels on row 2, data from row 3 in preorder with Excel outline levels 0 through 3, and a merged Grand Total last row. Amounts are NUMBERS rounded to the rupee with format rupee-hash-comma-zero - 107 numeric cells and 0 non-numeric in the Budget column - and the grand total reads 10050136 Budget against 11512712 Actual for July and 25913990 for FY-YTD, exactly the figures the statement shows on screen. Percentages are numbers with a 0.00% format, with 61 literal NA cells for nulls. verify.py passes.
commands_run: node tools/junit-run.mjs --file backend/src/mis/mis-statement-export.test.ts --name <each of four leaves> -> tests 1 / pass 1 / fail 0, testcase name = the leaf

host check: signed in through the real auth flow and called POST /api/mis/statement/export, saved 12,407 bytes, reopened with exceljs and inspected worksheet name, header rows, outline levels, cell types, number formats and totals
tests_added_or_updated: backend/src/mis/mis-statement-export.test.ts (the route's resolved/unresolvable branch and filename; the reopened workbook equal to the payload cell by cell; numbers, formats and one header group per present block; formula-injection neutralisation)
non_blocking_findings: The first generated workbook wrote the payload's RAW block labels ('2026-07-01', 'FY 26-27 YTD') where the screen shows 'July 2026' and 'FY 26-27 (YTD to Jul)' - export drift in the headings, found only by opening a really-generated file. The export now derives the heading from each block's from/to exactly as statement-view does, and the regenerated workbook agrees with the screen.
